### Velocity-Tuned Filters {#sec-velocityTunedFilters}

How can we measure input velocity? There are many different approaches in the computer vision community for measuring motion, and we will study them in @sec-motion_estimation. Here we show that it is possible to measure motion even with the simple processing machinery that we've developed so far.

We can use quadrature pairs of oriented filters in space-time to find
motion speed and direction in the video signal. We just need to find the
space-time orientation of strongest response. @fig-spacetimetiles2 (a)
shows a set of Gabor filters sampling the space-time frequency domain.
When the input contains a moving signal, we can use a set of filters to
identify the plane in the Fourier domain that contains the input energy.
@fig-spacetimetiles2 (b) shows the subset of filters that have the
strongest output for a particular input motion.

![](figures/temporal_filters/gabor_spacetime_tiles.png){width="100%" #fig-spacetimetiles2}

As an illustration, @fig-MT_velocity_tuned shows one possible
architecture to create velocity-selective units. The first layer is
composed by space-time Gabor filters (cosine and sine), which are
frequency-selective units. Here we represent the impulse response of
each filter by a small $x-y-t$ cube. For each quadrature pair we compute
the amplitude. Then amplitude outputs are combined according to form
different planes in the Fourier domain to create velocity-selective
outputs. A normalization layer can be added to normalize the outputs by
dividing every output by the sum of all the amplitudes (not shown). The
full architecture is nonlinear.

Given an input sequence, one can estimate velocity by looking at the
velocity-tuned unit with the strongest response.

demo_steps.narration: Reversing the direction of motion (vx = -1.0, vy = -1.0) tilts the plane in the opposite direction. The active filter subset shifts accordingly, illustrating how direction-selective units can be built by monitoring specific plane configurations.

interactionPlan.camera_suggestion: Elevated three-quarter orthographic view showing the top, front-left, and front-right faces of the grid cube, matching the original figure's perspective.
interactionPlan.view_reasoning: (1) The wx axis runs horizontally to the right and slightly downwards, the wt axis runs straight up, and the wy axis recedes into the page to the upper-right. (2) This receding depth axis direction implies the camera is positioned in the front-left quadrant (near -35 degrees azimuth) looking toward the origin, so that +X points right-down and -Z points right-up. (3) The top faces of the spheres are clearly visible, indicating a moderate elevation of about 25 degrees above the horizontal plane.

camera_view.view_notes: Perfect match for the textbook's oblique-style orthographic projection, showcasing the 3D grid shape and the tilted plane clearly.

inline_constraints.default_view: Must show the 3D grid of spheres with axes exactly matching the layout of panels (a) and (b).
inline_constraints.visible_ui: At most two compact sliders for vx and vy, placed unobtrusively near the edge.
inline_constraints.explainers: Use hover tooltips to show the (wx, wy, wt) coordinate of individual spheres and their distance to the current motion plane.
inline_constraints.framing: Maintain a generous margin around the grid so that labels and axis arrows do not get clipped during rotation.
inline_constraints.camera: Match the camera viewpoint closely on startup so that the user immediately recognizes the connection to the original figure.

interactionPlan.notes: Render the spheres with a metallic or highly-shaded Phong material to recreate the glossy 3D look of the original figure. Compute each sphere's distance to the plane dynamically: d = |vx*wx + vy*wy + wt| / sqrt(vx^2 + vy^2 + 1). Spheres with d < 0.3 should be fully opaque and colored deep metallic blue/grey; spheres with d >= 0.3 should smoothly fade to 0.15 opacity so the background grid structure remains visible as a reference.

evaluation.geometry_accuracy_analysis: The 3D reconstruction is highly accurate, utilizing real 3D SphereGeometry and CylinderGeometry/ConeGeometry for axes and a custom BufferGeometry for the velocity plane in orthographic projection. The side-by-side layout of panels (a) and (b) matches the source closely in scale, orientation, and perspective.
evaluation.geometry_accuracy_improvement: Slightly increase the spacing of the spheres in the grid to reduce overlap and match the airy density of the source diagram.
evaluation.interactivity_usability_analysis: The developer implemented several highly functional and pedagogically rich interactions: (1) Two compact sliders for vx and vy that dynamically tilt the 3D plane in real-time and recalculate the distance/opacity/scale of all 125 Gabor filter spheres; (2) Interactive individual filter spheres that, when clicked, display a detailed popup with their exact coordinate index and distance to the motion plane; (3) Click-to-cycle functionality on the motion-energy plane itself which steps through a 4-part guided demo with smooth interpolation transitions and descriptive narration popups; (4) Interactive axes and filter banks with custom educational tooltips explaining their physical meaning.
evaluation.faithfulness_analysis: The overall layout, including the two separate diagrams (a) and (b), axis arrows, and labels, is recognizable. However, diagram (b) features a chaotic 3D cluster of dark spheres intersecting the tilted plane, whereas the original displays a neat, coplanar 2D grid of uniform grey spheres lying flat on the plane surface.
discrepancies: Spheres in diagram (b) form a cluttered 3D cluster instead of a flat 2D grid on the plane.
The spheres in (b) are mismatched in color, appearing dark/black instead of uniform silver-grey.
Slight clipping and overlap issues in the 3D rendering of the lattice in (b).
evaluation.faithfulness_improvement: Align the spheres in diagram (b) into a clean, coplanar 5x5 grid positioned flat on the tilted plane, and match their material color to the silver-grey used in diagram (a).
evaluation.label_quality_analysis: Source labels include '(a)', '(b)', '$w_t$', '$w_x$', and '$w_y$' for both sub-figures. In the output, all labels are present and styled with matching math-italic fonts. The placement of '$w_x$' in sub-figure (a) is slightly cluttered as it overlaps with some of the sphere geometry near the axis end, and the direction of the axes varies slightly from the original projection, but overall readability is high.
evaluation.label_quality_improvement: Adjust the offset of the '$w_x$' label in sub-figure (a) to prevent overlap with the sphere elements.
evaluation.concept_accuracy_analysis: Core concept: Spatiotemporal Gabor filter banks and velocity tuning (frequency plane constraint $v_x\omega_x + v_y\omega_y + \omega_t = 0$). User-visible claims: (1) Sliders for $v_x$ and $v_y$ accurately tilt the 3D plane. (2) Distance calculation dynamically highlights only the Gabor spheres near the plane, matching the physical constraint. (3) Demo step texts and interactive tooltips correctly explain the relationship between spatial/temporal frequencies and pattern translation speed. No conceptual misalignments or errors are present.
evaluation.notes: The 3D figure features excellent interactive logic and a strong conceptual foundation, but falls short in faithfulness in panel (b). Instead of a flat, clean coplanar grid of uniform silver-grey spheres lying directly on the tilted plane, panel (b) renders a cluttered, dark 3D cluster of spheres with clipping issues. Improving sphere density, alignment, and coloring in panel (b) is the primary path to high fidelity.
action_items: In panel (b), project and restrict the visible spheres to a flat, coplanar 5x5 grid lying directly on the tilted motion-energy plane, matching the 2D layout of the source figure instead of a 3D cubic lattice.
Change the material colors of the spheres in panel (b) to the uniform silver-grey color used in panel (a) (0xaebebe) rather than the dark/black tones.
Increase the grid spacing constant of the spheres in both panels from 0.39 to approximately 0.46 to reduce mesh overlap and achieve the airy density of the source diagram.
Adjust the HTML label offset for the 'w_x' label in panel (a) to move it further to the right and prevent overlap with the boundary spheres.

feedback.rationale: The conceptual structure and interactivity are excellent, but the execution needs concrete implementation fixes in panel (b) regarding sphere layout, colors, spacing, and label offsets, which can be resolved by refining the generation.
